title: Grateful Dead Live at Labor Temple on 1969-02-02
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy early ’69 show with smoking Dark Star, Eleven and Other One, captured on a soundboard that’s uneven but listenable.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its soaring Jerry Garcia solos – especially on Dark Star, The Eleven and the intense Other One>Cryptical sequence – and for the raw psychedelic fire of Pigpen’s Lovelight.  The SBD source is uneven (high‑mid guitar focus, thin low end and a few splice/fade cuts) but most listeners consider it above‑average for the era and well worth the occasional mix hiccup.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (15/19) are 4‑5 stars highlighting superb musical moments; technical complaints are consistent but not severe, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Uneven mix with Jerry’s guitar high in the front and weak bottom‑end definition; occasional splice/fade in The Eleven and a brief cut at the end of that track.  Despite these issues the tape is considered above‑average for 1969 SBD recordings.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A tight, psychedelic set that moves from the soaring Dark Star into a blistering Eleven and then into an intense Other One>Cryptical, with Pigpen’s soulful Lovelight providing a powerful closer.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for inspired, tight guitar solos and a dominant tone that drives the show.
